name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.15.0 — a due reviewer replay is now EXECUTED by review's own close instead of printed as a reminder. `spec-review-driver.js` gains a REPLAY state between MERGE's conclusion and DONE: it runs `replay.js --due` and `--select` itself, and on a due window with a selectable target it refuses to conclude the review until a `stage:"replay"` ledger row exists for that target's `reviewRunId` — joined on the run id, never a bare row count, so a concurrent session's measurement cannot satisfy this review's mark. Any recorded outcome concludes it (a non-measurement outcome leaves the harness due, so the next review retries rather than this one), and REPLAY never re-derives, re-opens, or gates the verdict — CLOSE is committed and MERGE has concluded before it runs. Motivation is measured, not argued: the advisory form shipped 2026-08-19, printed `reviewer replay due` on every CLEAN report, and was skipped through 12+ reviews in ~48 hours in this repo alone — so the driver's own copy of that reminder is retired outright rather than made louder. Two mechanical consequences ride along: the `<spec>.review/` sidecar is now deleted at DONE rather than at MERGE (REPLAY reads it), and a worktree merge relocates its state file into the main root before `merge-back cleanup` runs, since REPLAY executes after the worktree is gone. `/spec:replay` remains the manual and retry surface; its phases live in `replay.md` alone and are invoked, never restated. Landed in the same version (JJ ruling, after a Fable 5 consult on this build's own recorded debts): agent memory becomes a disposed artifact rather than a silent one. core § Feedback Loop already claimed the pipeline improves "through artifacts — never through anyone's memory" while `.claude/agent-memory/` sat outside its carrier list — written by dispatched workers, steering the next worker before any gate can observe the effect, outliving its session, derived by nothing and reviewed by nothing. Review's close now disposes every memory file a spec's diff touched, one stated fate each (carry / correct / delete), judged on what it teaches. The trigger was this build shipping a false one: two memories from a single incident both attributed the orchestrator's own concurrent edits to a phantom sibling worker and both concluded the assignment could be stood down from — one was deleted at the time, its twin rode the same commit unexamined. Deliberately NOT built, and recorded as unearned under core § Incident Policy at a recurrence count of one: any memory-review gate, write hook, or lint over the directory. 7.14.2 — three `review.md` prose corrections, found by /spec:review of the driver spine's own spec (JJ + Fable 5 consult, 2026-08-21). The frozen-base check + detached-worktree add/remove, cut at build time, is retired outright rather than deferred: attributing foreign hunks to their owning spec (the driver's skip-name extraction) covers both the HEAD-moved-past case the mechanism targeted and the interleaved-concurrent case it structurally cannot see, so `review.md`'s false claim that the driver runs the check is removed and § Protocol now names the base-derivation rungs that actually shipped (`build_base` → `diff_base` → `merge-base HEAD main|master`). The `done`-spec re-run promise is retired: re-reviewing a `done` spec was walking the full stage with zero ledger append and zero retained evidence (`runId: undefined`), so a cold invocation on an already-closed spec is now refused (exit 2), pointing at `/spec:escape` — the command for a defect that escaped a review that already passed. The CLOSE step's close-commit text is corrected for worktree reviews: `.claude/spec-runs.jsonl` and `.claude/spec-runs/` are excluded from the close commit and promoted to the main root once the merge lands, since committing them inside the worktree left `merge-back cleanup` seeing a dirty tree and exiting 2 after the merge had already landed; in-place reviews are unaffected. 7.14.1 — smoke serializes behind every leg that can run host tests or build the app: `review-legs.js` wave 2 ran `smoke.sh` concurrently with the at-risk test dispatch and the patterns sweep, and a host at-risk test performing a real production build clobbered the artifact smoke was booting (UpWell 2026-08-21, 3/3 runs: ENOTEMPTY under `.nitro/vite` during the concurrent vite build, then readyCheck never passed — smoke alone green every time). This is the same collision class the 2026-08-17 wave-1 comment already documented for the gate, so smoke now runs in its own wave after at-risk/patterns/drift complete; two observed members, so an in-place fix, not a standing guard. Second defect from the same report: smoke's stdout/stderr were discarded entirely — a red smoke row carried no diagnosis and cost two extra full re-runs to identify — so the full output now lands in `<out-dir>/smoke.txt`, advertised on the outputs line. Pinned by a behavioral test whose fixture at-risk run sleeps then drops a marker the bootCommand probes for at boot start — red on the pre-fix concurrency by construction (verified against the stashed pre-fix script).
